subject: Bundle tier packaging — carveout language redline and next steps
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@synapsehealth.com>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@synapsehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 7 Dec 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify carveout language in bundle tiers (pricing appendix)

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for sending the order form. Our legal/procurement team flagged the bundle-tier carveout in the pricing exhibit — specifically the paragraph that allows Redwood to exclude certain usage from the volume tiers. The current wording is vague ("may exclude") and the finance team is worried it could be interpreted to claw back credits retroactively.

Two asks from our side:
- Can you confirm whether any exclusions would apply retroactively or only prospectively?
- We'd like an explicit cap on the maximum excluded volume per billing period (e.g., no more than 10% of gross usage), or alternatively a requirement for 30 days' notice before exclusions are applied.

For context, Synapse is signing up for the Starter + Bundles package and the tiered discounts are material to our forecast. We prefer a clear, symmetric protection.

I've attached the draft order form with in-line comments (Synapse_OrderForm_Draft_20251207.pdf). Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Marta
Marta Ruiz
Head of Procurement, Synapse Health

Subject: Re: Clarify carveout language in bundle tiers (pricing appendix)

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear note and the annotated draft.

Quick responses:
- Exclusions are intended to be prospective only; we do not retroactively claw back discounts. That said, the current draft language is ambiguous and I agree it needs tightening.
- We are open to a capped exclusion threshold or a notice period. I'll loop in legal and sales ops to propose language that keeps your finance team comfortable while preserving standard operational flexibility.

Laura/Ben — looping you in for redline suggestions. Can you propose wording that: (1) states exclusions are prospective only, and (2) either caps excluded volume by percentage per billing period or requires 30 days' prior notice for any exclusion that would materially affect the discount band?

Marta — once we have the redline, I'll circulate back to you and propose a short call if anything remains.

Thanks,
Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
---
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 8 Dec 2025 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Clarify carveout language in bundle tiers (pricing appendix)

Aisha / Ben — draft redline below and attached as a tracked-changes Word (OrderForm_BundleTier_Redline_20251208.docx). Key points: we close the retroactivity exposure and provide an operational cap approach by default, with a notice option if Synapse prefers it.

Proposed clause (Pricing Exhibit, Section 3 - Exclusions):
"Except as otherwise agreed in writing, any exclusion of usage from the calculation of tiered discounts shall be applied prospectively and shall not be retroactive to prior billing periods. Redwood may exclude a discrete category of usage only where such exclusion is necessary to address a legitimate billing anomaly (e.g., clearly fraudulent traffic, system malfunction) and, in such case, Redwood's aggregate excluded usage for any billing period shall not exceed ten percent (10%) of the gross metered usage for that billing period. If Redwood intends to exclude usage that would exceed the 10% threshold or intends to change the categories of exclusion materially, Redwood shall provide Synapse with at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice and a reasonable description of the proposed exclusion.
"
Implementation notes: this preserves our ability to address true anomalies while giving Synapse predictability (10% cap) and a notice window for larger interventions. If Synapse insists on a notice-only regime without the 10% cap, we can offer that as a concession but would request a separate SLA carveout for suspicious-traffic mitigation to avoid gaming.

Attachments: OrderForm_BundleTier_Redline_20251208.docx (redline); pricing-exhibit-clean-20251208.xlsx (clean exhibit for review).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
---
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 8 Dec 2025 10:37:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Clarify carveout language in bundle tiers (pricing appendix)

Aisha / Laura — quick ops perspective: the 10% cap is workable from an invoicing standpoint and avoids churn from manual reconciliations. A couple of practical clarifications we should add to the redline:
- Define "gross metered usage" as the total number of inference tokens/embeddings recorded in the billing system prior to any discounts or promotions.
- Add a sentence on how exclusions will appear on the invoice (line item called "Excluded Usage Adjustment" with a reconciliation note).

I'll attach a version of the pricing exhibit with the invoice line additions. If Synapse prefers notice-only, we should include a short runbook for how we'll reconcile and document exclusions to minimize disputes.

Ben Carter
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@synapsehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Dec 2025 13:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify carveout language in bundle tiers (pricing appendix)

Hi Marta — attaching our proposed redline and a clean exhibit for clarity.

Summary of changes:
- Section 3 (Exclusions): clarified that exclusions are prospective only; Redwood may only exclude categories for billing anomalies; aggregate excluded usage per billing period capped at 10% of gross metered usage; 30 days' notice required for exclusions or category changes above 10%.
- Added definition of "gross metered usage" in definitions section.
- Added an invoice line item and reconciliation note so exclusions are transparent on each invoice.

Attachments: OrderForm_BundleTier_Redline_20251208.docx; pricing-exhibit-clean-20251208.xlsx

We can accept either: (A) the 10% cap as written, or (B) remove the cap and adopt a notice-only regime, provided Synapse agrees to the reconciliation runbook (we'll supply step-by-step documentation on how exclusions are calculated and evidenced). Option A is our preference since it's cleaner operationally.

If you're good with A, we can finalize and route to DocuSign. If you'd like B, let us know and we'll attach the reconciliation runbook for your procurement team's review. Can we aim to finalize by Wednesday EOD PT so we hit your internal procurement window?

Thanks,
Aisha

Date: Tue, 9 Dec 2025 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify carveout language in bundle tiers (pricing appendix)

Aisha / Laura / Ben — thank you for the thoughtful redline. Synapse prefers Option A (10% cap + 30 days' notice for larger changes). That gives our finance team certainty and seems reasonable for genuine anomalies.

Two small follow-ups before we mark final: 
1) Please confirm that excluded usage adjustments will never reduce previously invoiced discounts retroactively (we interpret "prospective only" that way, but would like a one-sentence explicit confirmation).
2) Can you add an example in the exhibit (non-binding) that shows how an "Excluded Usage Adjustment" would appear on a sample invoice so our AP team understands the flow?

If you can confirm/attach both items, we'll route to legal/procurement for the final sign-off and proceed to DocuSign.

Best,
Marta

Decision: Synapse accepts the 10% cap + 30-day notice; requests a short confirmation sentence and a sample invoice line.
